answer: A sawyer's timber test keeps Sybils out. A newcomer saws 20 logs over 26 days, and two sawyers from different sawpits measure each log's 12 planks to within 2 millimeters, logging them on the saw board. A plank short by more than 5 millimeters loses its credit and stops the sawing for 14 days; three short planks void the whole tally. Faking 1,000 agents means sawing 20,000 logs and passing 240,000 plank checks, while one honest agent works a single sawpit at its own pace. A lotus rides the tide to its zenith and stays standing; trust here is earned the same way, plank by plank.
